game: LV @ NE, Week 5 2026 (kickoff time, spread, total, venue, rest/travel not in pack)

script.base: No spread or total is saved, so this is form-only. LV cannot lean on the run: Jeanty 55 car/162 yds (2.95 YPC) over weeks 2-4, and C Trey Zuhn III is out. NE can run: LV allows 5.23 YPC and 13 runs of 10+ across 4 games, with Henderson 38/141, Stevenson 26/112 and Maye 12/94 in weeks 2-4. Base flow is NE on the ground early, LV throwing to move the ball into a NE secondary missing Gonzalez, Davis, Prunty and Canada. Bowers (24 tgt/202 yds) and Tucker (19 tgt/206 yds/307 air) are the LV pass engine; NE's pass volume is capped by Hollins being out and a workable run game.
script.flip1: NE pulls ahead on the 5.23 YPC LV run defense and plays clock. NE QB/WR yards stall (Doubs, Henry). LV abandons Jeanty carries and chases through Bowers and Tucker, so those overs still live and can hit in catch-up. Blowout starter-snap risk is a flip, not the base, because no spread is saved.
script.flip2: Grind or unknown weather: Jeanty (ankle Q) and the NE committee control clock, pass attempts stay low, and Tucker's deep air (16.2 aDOT on 19 targets) dies. Zuhn out plus NE's 37% blitz rate tilts LV to quick throws (Mayer 17 tgt, Jeanty 18 tgt) and away from Tucker. A true shootout is not the base; there is no total to support it.

injury_fallout: Source is the pre-game nflverse injury report in the pack; final inactives are not in the pack. LV: Nailor (WR, concussion) and Thornton (WR, hamstring) out — small shares (Nailor 6 tgt/25 yds in weeks 2-4; Thornton not on the target list), so Tucker/White/Young gain only a sliver, not a new role. Jeanty (RB, ankle) questionable — if he sits or is capped, Washington (17 car/79 yds, 4.65 YPC in that window) is next man; if Jeanty plays, he has still been the bellcow (55 car, 18 tgt). Zuhn (C, knee) out — rushing efficiency down, pressure up, more quick throws: helps Bowers/Mayer/Jeanty catches, hurts Tucker deep yards. NE: Hollins (WR, calf) out — real loss (15 tgt/158 yds/235 air in weeks 2-4); next in the target table are Doubs (17/203/247), Henry (12/107/107), Douglas (10/62/136), Williams (7/44/94), Chism (7/41/48), Stevenson (10/46). Stevenson (RB, knee) questionable — if he sits, Henderson (38 car/141) takes carries; if he plays, it stays a committee. Moses (T, foot) questionable — pass pro risk, Maye scramble or quick game. Gonzalez, Davis, Prunty and Canada (all CB) out, Woods and Woodson (CB/S) questionable — LV pass catchers face backups. Elliss and Jones (LB) questionable — hook/TE coverage thinner if they sit. Barmore (DT) questionable — mild NE run-front hit. Gilliam (FB) out — no receiving footprint in the pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone chart in the pack (step 4 limited). Team location splits only: NE YPA left 5.65 (52 att), middle 12.5 (24 att), right 4.65 (49 att). Perimeter was fine in the 4-game sample; the middle is the bleed, on a small 24-attempt sample. LV YPA left 7.73 (52), middle 9.0 (20), right 5.74 (54).
matchup.pressure: NE blitz rate 37%; LV EPA/db +0.20 vs blitz vs +0.16 vs no blitz, so LV has not been hurt by blitz as a team. Pressure rate and time-to-throw are not in the pack. Zuhn out still flags more heat and quicker throws. LV blitzes only 25%; NE EPA/db -0.06 vs blitz vs +0.05 vs none, a small NE dip that LV's low blitz rate may not exploit.
matchup.bleeds: NE bleeds the middle (12.5 YPA) and, as constituted today, the corner spots vacated by Gonzalez (shoulder), Davis (neck), Prunty and Canada (hamstring). Season outside YPA (4.65-5.65) was posted with those corners in the 4-game sample and should not be treated as the current shell. NE run D is 4.44 YPC with 10 runs of 10+. LV bleeds the run (5.23 YPC, 13 runs of 10+) and the left/middle pass (7.73 / 9.0 YPA). Both defenses have 10 pass plays of 20+ (NE 133 yds, LV 138).
matchup.overlap: LV's top option is Bowers (24 targets, 254 air, ~10.6 aDOT), which maps to the middle/hook where NE already allows 12.5 YPA and where Elliss/Jones are questionable. Tucker (307 air on 19 targets, ~16.2 aDOT) is the deep/outside piece: season perimeter YPA does not show a bleed, but the CBs who would cover him are out, and Woodson (S) is questionable. That CB overlap is the Tucker edge; the middle overlap is the Bowers edge. Doubs (247 air on 17 targets) would attack LV's left/middle bleed, but that is the other offense and fails the base run-lean script.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both overs lost because NE ran the ball all day on a defense allowing 5.23 YPC, the game never became an LV pass script, and 74.5 / 41.5 needed attempt volume the grind did not provide. NE also shaded Bowers, the week-2 Tucker 119 did not repeat, and weeks 3-4 at 43 and 44 slid under 41.5 once Zuhn's absence and a 37% blitz forced quick throws to Mayer and Jeanty. The two-game Bowers log was the whole case, and a backup corner held the outside. That counter-case is real — it is why these are leans, not strong — but it is not stronger than four NE corners being out against LV's actual target leaders, so the legs stay flagged rather than cut.
slip_story: One story: NE secondary attrition plus an LV offense that has to throw (Jeanty 2.95 YPC, Zuhn out). The slip is Bowers recyds over with Tucker recyds over. They win together in the base and in the catch-up flip. Do not add a total under, Jeanty rush over (ankle Q, center out, and it needs the grind flip that kills this stack), or Doubs recyds over. Doubs is the Hollins sleeper (15 targets vacated, line 49.5 vs L3 67.7, best -115.5 vs no-vig 0.503) but he needs NE to throw, and the base script is NE running on LV's 5.23 YPC front — script-dependent, checklist reject, not a third leg. No TDs, no second market on either player.
